column1: # Error-reporting corpus. One case per row, tab-separated. Lines starting with # are comments.
# Columns: id <TAB> file <TAB> sybase <TAB> mssql <TAB> postgres <TAB> must_contain
# Each platform cell is either:
#   ok                 the statement must succeed (exit 0, no "Msg " line)
#   error:<substring>  the statement must fail (exit non-zero) AND print <substring>
#                      EXACTLY ONCE (a second copy means the error is being reported
#                      twice -- once via the driver's info-message channel and once via
#                      the exception it also raises)
#   n/a                the case does not apply to this platform
# The substrings are the server's own message numbers, so they are stable across
# releases and locales in a way the message TEXT is not.
# must_contain is a pipe-separated list of substrings that must ALL appear in the
# output, checked only on the platforms where the case is expected to succeed. It is
# how a case asserts that every platform renders the same values -- use `-` for none.
id
overflow
divide-by-zero
bad-convert
error-after-rows
missing-table
raiserror
money-and-decimal
decimal-scales
